Object._: The settings of one thing in your scene: where it sits, how it is turned and sized, how it is shown, and who it is parented to.
Object.use_fake_user: Keeps this item saved in the file even if nothing uses it. Without it, unused items are deleted when you save and reopen.
Object.use_extra_user: An internal flag that marks the item as having one more user. Normally you never need to touch it.
Object.is_runtime_data: Marks data that Blender builds while running and does not save in the .blend file. Mostly for add-on developers.
Object.tag: A scratch flag that tools use to mark data for their own work. Its starting value is not reliable, so ignore it.
Object.parent_type: Chooses what kind of thing this object is attached to, like a whole object, a bone or a single vertex.
Object.parent_type.OBJECT: Attached to another whole object. It follows that object's moves, turns and scaling.
Object.parent_type.ARMATURE: Attached to a skeleton (armature) so the skeleton's bones can deform and move this object.
Object.parent_type.LATTICE: Attached to a lattice, a cage of points, so it bends when the cage bends.
Object.parent_type.VERTEX: Attached to one single point (vertex) of another mesh. It rides along with that point.
Object.parent_type.VERTEX_3: Attached to three vertices of another mesh, so it follows both their position and their rotation.
Object.parent_type.BONE: Attached to one bone of a skeleton. It moves whenever that bone moves.
Object.parent_vertices: The numbers of the mesh points this object is stuck to when parented to vertices.
Object.parent_bone: The name of the bone this object is attached to when parented to a bone.
Object.parent_bone_head_tail_factor: Where along the parent bone the object sits. 0 is the bone's base (head), 1 is its tip (tail).
Object.use_parent_final_indices: Uses vertex numbers after modifiers have changed the parent mesh, not the original ones. Use when modifiers change vertex order.
Object.use_camera_lock_parent: While View Lock to Camera is on, moving the view moves the camera's parent instead of the camera itself.
Object.track_axis: Which of the object's own directions points forward. Used when it must face something or align to vertices.
Object.track_axis.POS_X: The object's positive X direction counts as forward.
Object.track_axis.POS_Y: The object's positive Y direction counts as forward.
Object.track_axis.POS_Z: The object's positive Z direction counts as forward.
Object.track_axis.NEG_X: The object's negative X direction counts as forward.
Object.track_axis.NEG_Y: The object's negative Y direction counts as forward.
Object.track_axis.NEG_Z: The object's negative Z direction counts as forward.
Object.up_axis: Which of the object's own directions points up. Works with Track Axis to fix how the object is turned.
Object.up_axis.X: The object's X direction counts as up.
Object.up_axis.Y: The object's Y direction counts as up.
Object.up_axis.Z: The object's Z direction counts as up.
Object.active_material_index: Which material slot is currently selected in the list. Painting or assigning affects this slot.
Object.location: Where the object is in the 3D world, as X, Y and Z positions (left/right, front/back, up/down).
Object.rotation_quaternion: The object's turn stored as four numbers (W, X, Y, Z). Avoids gimbal lock, but is hard to edit by hand.
Object.rotation_axis_angle: The object's turn stored as an angle plus an axis to spin around, like turning a doorknob around a pole.
Object.rotation_euler: How far the object is turned around the X, Y and Z axes, in degrees. The easiest rotation to understand.
Object.rotation_mode: Chooses how the object's rotation is stored and edited. Values from the other modes are ignored.
Object.rotation_mode.QUATERNION: Four-number rotation that never locks up (no gimbal lock). Best for smooth animation.
Object.rotation_mode.XYZ: Turns around X first, then Y, then Z. The default. Can lock up when two axes line up (gimbal lock).
Object.rotation_mode.XZY: Turns in the order X, Z, Y. Can suffer gimbal lock when two axes line up.
Object.rotation_mode.YXZ: Turns in the order Y, X, Z. Can suffer gimbal lock when two axes line up.
Object.rotation_mode.YZX: Turns in the order Y, Z, X. Can suffer gimbal lock when two axes line up.
Object.rotation_mode.ZXY: Turns in the order Z, X, Y. Can suffer gimbal lock when two axes line up.
Object.rotation_mode.ZYX: Turns in the order Z, Y, X. Can suffer gimbal lock when two axes line up.
Object.rotation_mode.AXIS_ANGLE: Rotates by an angle around a chosen direction line (axis). Handy to spin around any custom axis.
Object.scale: How big the object is along X, Y and Z. 1 is normal size, 2 is double, 0.5 is half.
Object.dimensions: The real width, depth and height of the object's box. Editing it changes the scale to match.
Object.delta_location: An extra position offset added on top of Location. Handy for shifting animated objects without editing keys.
Object.delta_rotation_euler: An extra turn added on top of the normal Euler rotation, without changing the main rotation values.
Object.delta_rotation_quaternion: An extra turn added on top of the quaternion rotation, without changing the main rotation values.
Object.delta_scale: An extra size multiplier added on top of Scale, without changing the main scale values.
Object.lock_location: Stops you from moving the object along the ticked axes when you drag or type transforms.
Object.lock_rotation: Stops you from turning the object around the ticked axes when you transform it.
Object.lock_rotation_w: Locks the angle part of a four-number rotation so it cannot be changed while transforming.
Object.lock_rotations_4d: Locks each of the four rotation numbers separately instead of treating them as a normal turn.
Object.lock_scale: Stops you from resizing the object along the ticked axes when you transform it.
Object.matrix_world: A table of numbers that holds the object's final position, turn and size in the whole world. For scripting.
Object.matrix_local: The object's position, turn and size relative to its parent only. For scripting.
Object.matrix_basis: The object's own position, turn and size before parents and constraints change them. For scripting.
Object.matrix_parent_inverse: A saved correction that keeps the object in place at the moment it was parented. For scripting.
Object.empty_display_type: Chooses the shape an Empty (an invisible helper object) shows in the viewport. It never renders.
Object.empty_display_type.PLAIN_AXES: Draws a simple 3D cross, like a plus sign.
Object.empty_display_type.ARROWS: Draws three arrows showing the X, Y and Z directions.
Object.empty_display_type.SINGLE_ARROW: Draws one arrow pointing along the empty's Z axis.
Object.empty_display_type.IMAGE: Shows a picture in the viewport, useful as a drawing reference.
Object.empty_display_size: How big the empty's shape is drawn in the viewport. Only changes the look, not the real object size.
Object.empty_image_offset: Moves the image sideways so its middle (the pivot) is not exactly at the empty's origin.
Object.empty_image_depth: Decides whether other objects can cover the reference image or the image draws over them.
Object.empty_image_depth.DEFAULT: The image hides and is hidden like a normal object, based on distance.
Object.empty_image_depth.FRONT: The image always draws in front of other objects.
Object.empty_image_depth.BACK: The image always draws behind other objects.
Object.show_empty_image_perspective: Shows the reference image when you look through the normal perspective view (things get smaller far away).
Object.show_empty_image_orthographic: Shows the reference image in orthographic views, which have no perspective, like front and top.
Object.show_empty_image_only_axis_aligned: Only shows the image when you look straight at it along one axis, like a front or side blueprint.
Object.use_empty_image_alpha: Blends see-through parts of the image smoothly. May cause flicker where several images overlap.
Object.empty_image_side: Chooses which face of the flat image you can see.
Object.empty_image_side.DOUBLE_SIDED: The image is visible from the front and from the back.
Object.empty_image_side.FRONT: The image is visible only from the front.
Object.empty_image_side.BACK: The image is visible only from the back.
Object.add_rest_position_attribute: Saves a copy of every point's position before shape keys change it, so Geometry Nodes can use the original.
Object.pass_index: A number you give the object so render passes can pick it out. Used for masks in compositing.
Object.color: The object's tint and see-through amount, shown in the viewport when the Object color mode is on.
Object.use_simulation_cache: Remembers simulation results frame by frame so playing back is fast. Turn off to save memory.
Object.hide_viewport: Hides the object in all 3D viewports completely. It can still show in the final render.
Object.hide_select: Stops the object from being clicked or box-selected, so you cannot move it by accident.
Object.hide_render: Leaves the object out of final renders. It still shows in the viewport.
Object.hide_probe_volume: Makes volume light probes ignore this object when they bake lighting (EEVEE).
Object.hide_probe_sphere: Makes sphere reflection probes ignore this object when they capture reflections (EEVEE).
Object.hide_probe_plane: Makes planar reflection probes ignore this object when they capture reflections (EEVEE).
Object.hide_surface_pick: Stops the object from helping tools that snap to or pick the surface under your mouse.
Object.show_instancer_for_render: When this object makes copies of others, still draw this original in the final render.
Object.show_instancer_for_viewport: When this object makes copies of others, still draw this original in the viewport.
Object.visible_camera: If off, camera rays pass through the object so you cannot see it directly, but it can still cast shadows and light.
Object.visible_diffuse: If off, the object does not bounce soft light onto others (diffuse rays pass through it).
Object.visible_glossy: If off, the object does not show up in shiny reflections on other objects.
Object.visible_transmission: If off, the object does not show through glass or other see-through materials.
Object.visible_volume_scatter: If off, the object is ignored by light scattering inside fog and smoke.
Object.visible_shadow: If off, the object casts no shadow, but is still visible.
Object.is_holdout: Cuts a see-through hole in the render where the object is. Used to mix renders with other footage.
Object.is_shadow_catcher: The object shows only shadows and reflections falling on it, so you can place 3D things in real photos.
Object.visible_raycast: If off, effects that trace rays against the scene (like some EEVEE ones) ignore this object.
Object.instance_type: Lets this object make copies of its children, on every point or face, or of a whole collection.
Object.instance_type.NONE: No copies are made. The object behaves normally.
Object.instance_type.VERTS: Child objects are copied onto every vertex of this mesh.
Object.instance_type.FACES: Child objects are copied onto every face of this mesh.
Object.instance_type.COLLECTION: A whole collection is placed here as a copy, like a stamp of a group of objects.
Object.use_instance_vertices_rotation: Turns each copy so it follows the surface direction (normal) at its vertex.
Object.use_instance_faces_scale: Makes each copy bigger or smaller to match the size of the face it sits on.
Object.instance_faces_scale: A size multiplier for copies placed on faces. Low shrinks them, high grows them.
Object.display_type: How the object is drawn in the 3D viewport. It does not change how it renders.
Object.display_type.BOUNDS: Only shows the box around the object. Very fast for heavy objects.
Object.display_type.WIRE: Shows only the edges as lines, like a wire cage.
Object.display_type.SOLID: Shows the object as a plain filled shape with simple lighting.
Object.display_type.TEXTURED: Shows the object with its textures and colors.
Object.show_bounds: Draws a box (or other shape) around the whole object so you can see its size.
Object.display_bounds_type: Chooses the shape used for the bounds outline.
Object.display_bounds_type.BOX: Draws the bounds as a box.
Object.display_bounds_type.SPHERE: Draws the bounds as a ball.
Object.display_bounds_type.CYLINDER: Draws the bounds as a can-shaped cylinder.
Object.display_bounds_type.CONE: Draws the bounds as a cone.
Object.display_bounds_type.CAPSULE: Draws the bounds as a pill shape with round ends.
Object.show_name: Shows the object's name as text next to it in the viewport.
Object.show_axis: Draws the object's origin dot and its X, Y, Z direction lines in the viewport.
Object.show_texture_space: Draws the box that texture coordinates are measured against, handy for fixing stretched textures.
Object.show_wire: Draws the edges as lines on top of the solid surface.
Object.show_all_edges: Shows every edge of the mesh, including ones normally hidden because they sit between flat faces.
Object.use_grease_pencil_lights: Lets scene lights shade this Grease Pencil drawing instead of flat color.
Object.show_transparent: Shows see-through materials as see-through in the viewport.
Object.show_in_front: Draws the object on top of everything else, even if other objects are in front of it.
Object.show_only_shape_key: Shows only the selected shape key at full strength, so you can check it alone.
Object.use_shape_key_edit_mode: Shows the shape key's shape while editing the mesh in Edit Mode.
Object.active_shape_key_index: Which shape key is currently selected in the list.
Object.use_mesh_mirror_x: Edits on one side of the mesh are copied to the other side across the X axis (left/right).
Object.use_mesh_mirror_y: Edits on one side of the mesh are copied to the other side across the Y axis (front/back).
Object.use_mesh_mirror_z: Edits on one side of the mesh are copied to the other side across the Z axis (up/down).
Object.lightgroup: Name of a light group this object belongs to, so its lighting renders as a separate layer you can adjust later.
Object.shadow_terminator_normal_offset: Fixes ugly dark shadow edges on low-poly smooth shapes. Low is off, higher pushes rays out; too high detaches shadows.
Object.shadow_terminator_geometry_offset: Another fix for jagged shadow edges on low-poly shapes. Higher values fix more but can leak light.
Object.shadow_terminator_shading_offset: Pushes the shadow edge toward the light to hide blocky look on low-poly smooth shapes. Higher hides more.
Object.active_selection_set: Which saved group of selected items (a selection set) is currently active.

Mesh._: The shape data of a 3D mesh: its points, edges and faces, plus remesh, symmetry and texture-space settings.
Mesh.use_fake_user: Keeps this item saved in the file even if nothing uses it. Without it, unused items are deleted when you save and reopen.
Mesh.use_extra_user: An internal flag that marks the item as having one more user. Normally you never need to touch it.
Mesh.is_runtime_data: Marks data that Blender builds while running and does not save in the .blend file. Mostly for add-on developers.
Mesh.tag: A scratch flag that tools use to mark data for their own work. Its starting value is not reliable, so ignore it.
Mesh.uv_layer_clone_index: Which UV map the Clone brush copies from when painting textures. Counts from 0.
Mesh.uv_layer_stencil_index: Which UV map is used as the mask when painting through a stencil. Counts from 0.
Mesh.remesh_voxel_size: Size of the little cubes used to rebuild the mesh. Low keeps fine detail but is slow; high is blocky but fast.
Mesh.remesh_voxel_adaptivity: Lets the remesh use fewer faces on flat parts. 0 keeps an even grid; higher gives fewer faces but less even ones.
Mesh.use_remesh_fix_poles: Tries to reduce spots where many edges meet (poles), so the new mesh flows better.
Mesh.use_remesh_preserve_volume: Pushes the new mesh back onto the original surface so its volume and details stay close.
Mesh.use_remesh_preserve_attributes: Copies all extra data (colors, UVs and so on) from the old mesh to the new one.
Mesh.remesh_mode: Chooses how the mesh is rebuilt into new clean geometry.
Mesh.remesh_mode.VOXEL: Rebuilds the mesh from small cubes. Great for sculpting; makes an even, dense mesh.
Mesh.remesh_mode.QUAD: Rebuilds the mesh using four-sided faces that follow the shape, giving cleaner topology.
Mesh.use_mirror_x: Mirrors changes across the X axis, so left and right sides stay the same while you sculpt or paint.
Mesh.use_mirror_y: Mirrors changes across the Y axis, so front and back stay the same while you sculpt or paint.
Mesh.use_mirror_z: Mirrors changes across the Z axis, so top and bottom stay the same while you sculpt or paint.
Mesh.use_mirror_vertex_groups: When painting weights, also paints the matching left or right vertex group (like Arm.L and Arm.R).
Mesh.radial_symmetry: Repeats your strokes in a circle around the center. The number is how many copies, like slices of a pie.
Mesh.use_auto_texspace: Resizes the texture box automatically to fit the object whenever it changes.
Mesh.use_mirror_topology: Mirrors using the mesh's shape connections instead of position. Needs both sides to match in structure.
Mesh.use_paint_bone_selection: Lets you pick bones to limit weight painting to the bones you select.
Mesh.use_paint_mask: In painting modes, only lets you paint on the faces you have selected.
Mesh.use_paint_mask_vertex: In painting modes, only lets you paint around the vertices you have selected.
Mesh.auto_texspace: Resizes the texture box automatically to fit the object whenever it changes.
Mesh.texspace_location: Where the texture box is placed. Moves how generated textures sit on the object.
Mesh.texspace_size: How big the texture box is. Larger spreads textures out, smaller makes them repeat more.

Camera._: The settings of a camera: lens, field of view, clipping range, special lens types and the guides shown in camera view.
Camera.use_fake_user: Keeps this item saved in the file even if nothing uses it. Without it, unused items are deleted when you save and reopen.
Camera.use_extra_user: An internal flag that marks the item as having one more user. Normally you never need to touch it.
Camera.is_runtime_data: Marks data that Blender builds while running and does not save in the .blend file. Mostly for add-on developers.
Camera.tag: A scratch flag that tools use to mark data for their own work. Its starting value is not reliable, so ignore it.
Camera.type: Chooses how the camera sees the world: normal perspective, flat orthographic, a wide panorama or a custom shader.
Camera.type.PERSP: Normal camera view where far things look smaller, like your eyes or a phone.
Camera.type.ORTHO: No perspective: parallel lines stay parallel. Used for technical drawings and isometric looks.
Camera.type.PANO: Wide special lenses like fisheye or 360 degree views, available in Cycles.
Camera.type.CUSTOM: Uses your own shader code to define how rays leave the camera. For advanced users.
Camera.sensor_fit: Decides whether the sensor size is measured by width, height, or whichever is bigger for your image shape.
Camera.sensor_fit.AUTO: Uses the sensor width for wide images and the height for tall images.
Camera.sensor_fit.HORIZONTAL: Always fits the field of view to the sensor width.
Camera.sensor_fit.VERTICAL: Always fits the field of view to the sensor height.
Camera.passepartout_alpha: How dark the shaded area outside the camera frame is. 0 is clear, 1 is fully black.
Camera.angle_x: How wide the camera sees from left to right, in degrees. Bigger means a wider view.
Camera.angle_y: How much the camera sees from top to bottom, in degrees. Bigger means a taller view.
Camera.angle: How wide the camera's view is, in degrees. Low zooms in like a telephoto lens, high looks wide.
Camera.clip_start: Closest distance the camera can see. Anything nearer than this is cut away. Too big removes close objects.
Camera.clip_end: Farthest distance the camera can see. Anything farther disappears. Too small cuts off the background.
Camera.lens: Focal length in millimeters. Low (18) is wide and sees a lot, high (200) zooms in on distant things.
Camera.sensor_width: Width of the camera's imaginary film or sensor in mm. A bigger sensor with the same lens sees a wider view.
Camera.sensor_height: Height of the camera's imaginary film or sensor in mm. Together with lens, it sets the vertical view.
Camera.ortho_scale: For orthographic cameras, how much of the world fits in the frame. Higher shows more, like zooming out.
Camera.display_size: How big the camera icon looks in the 3D viewport. It does not affect the render.
Camera.shift_x: Slides the view left or right without turning the camera. Useful to keep buildings straight.
Camera.shift_y: Slides the view up or down without turning the camera. Useful to keep vertical lines parallel.
Camera.show_limits: Draws the clip range and focus point on the camera so you can see where it sees and focuses.
Camera.show_mist: Draws a line showing where the mist (distance fog) starts and ends in the world.
Camera.show_passepartout: Darkens the area outside the camera frame in camera view, so you can focus on the final image.
Camera.show_safe_areas: Shows guide boxes marking the area where titles and action stay visible on TVs.
Camera.show_safe_center: Shows guides for cropping to another shape (like 4:3 from 16:9) without losing the main content.
Camera.show_name: Shows the camera's name in the corner of the camera view.
Camera.show_sensor: Draws the sensor frame in camera view, showing the real film area used.
Camera.show_background_images: Shows reference images placed behind objects in the 3D view.
Camera.lens_unit: Picks whether the lens is entered in millimeters or as a field of view angle.
Camera.lens_unit.MILLIMETERS: Enter the lens as focal length in millimeters, like a real camera lens.
Camera.lens_unit.FOV: Enter the lens as a viewing angle in degrees.
Camera.composition_guide_color: The color and transparency of the composition guide lines drawn in camera view.
Camera.show_composition_center: Draws lines through the middle of the frame to help center your subject.
Camera.show_composition_center_diagonal: Draws diagonal lines through the frame center to help place the subject.
Camera.show_composition_thirds: Draws a 3x3 grid. Placing subjects on the lines or crossings usually looks balanced.
Camera.show_composition_golden: Draws guides based on the golden ratio, a classic proportion for pleasing layouts.
Camera.show_composition_golden_tria_a: Draws a golden triangle guide, a diagonal layout that leads the eye through the frame.
Camera.show_composition_golden_tria_b: Draws the mirrored golden triangle guide, running the opposite diagonal.
Camera.show_composition_harmony_tri_a: Draws a harmonious triangle guide for placing subjects along a diagonal.
Camera.show_composition_harmony_tri_b: Draws the mirrored harmonious triangle guide, running the opposite diagonal.
Camera.panorama_type: Chooses which special wide lens shape Cycles uses when the camera type is Panoramic.
Camera.panorama_type.EQUIRECTANGULAR: A full 360 degree sphere flattened to a rectangle, like a world map. Used for VR and HDRIs.
Camera.panorama_type.EQUIANGULAR_CUBEMAP_FACE: Renders one face of a cube-shaped 360 view, with even angles across it.
Camera.panorama_type.MIRRORBALL: Mimics the view in a chrome ball, used to make environment maps.
Camera.panorama_type.FISHEYE_EQUIDISTANT: Fisheye where distance from center matches angle. Ideal for planetarium domes and ignores sensor size.
Camera.panorama_type.FISHEYE_EQUISOLID: Fisheye like most real lenses. It does use the sensor size.
Camera.panorama_type.FISHEYE_LENS_POLYNOMIAL: Fisheye defined by a math formula so you can copy a real lens's distortion.
Camera.panorama_type.CENTRAL_CYLINDRICAL: Wraps the view onto a cylinder around the camera, for wide panoramas.
Camera.fisheye_fov: How wide the fisheye lens sees, in degrees. 180 sees a half sphere.
Camera.fisheye_lens: Fisheye focal length in mm. Lower values give a stronger, wider fisheye effect.
Camera.latitude_min: Lowest angle seen up or down by the 360 camera. Raising it crops the bottom of the view.
Camera.latitude_max: Highest angle seen up or down by the 360 camera. Lowering it crops the top of the view.
Camera.longitude_min: Left edge of the horizontal angle the 360 camera sees. Narrow it to render only part of the circle.
Camera.longitude_max: Right edge of the horizontal angle the 360 camera sees. Narrow it to render only part of the circle.
Camera.fisheye_polynomial_k0: First number of the lens formula. Part of matching a real lens's distortion.
Camera.fisheye_polynomial_k1: Second number of the lens formula. Mostly controls the basic zoom of the lens.
Camera.fisheye_polynomial_k2: Third number of the lens formula. Adds curved distortion toward the edges.
Camera.fisheye_polynomial_k3: Fourth number of the lens formula. Fine tunes distortion near the frame edges.
Camera.fisheye_polynomial_k4: Fifth number of the lens formula. Finest tuning of the edge distortion.
Camera.central_cylindrical_range_u_min: Left limit of the horizontal angle seen by the cylindrical camera.
Camera.central_cylindrical_range_u_max: Right limit of the horizontal angle seen by the cylindrical camera.
Camera.central_cylindrical_range_v_min: Bottom limit of the height seen by the cylindrical camera.
Camera.central_cylindrical_range_v_max: Top limit of the height seen by the cylindrical camera.
Camera.central_cylindrical_radius: Radius of the imaginary cylinder around the camera. Changes how stretched the result looks.
Camera.custom_filepath: Where the custom camera shader file lives on your disk.
Camera.custom_mode: Chooses whether the custom camera shader comes from a text inside Blender or an outside file.
Camera.custom_mode.INTERNAL: Uses a text block stored inside the .blend file.
Camera.custom_mode.EXTERNAL: Reads the shader from a separate file on your computer.
Camera.custom_bytecode: The compiled version of the custom camera shader. Generated by Blender, not for editing.
Camera.custom_bytecode_hash: A short fingerprint of the compiled shader, used to quickly check if it changed.

CameraDOFSettings._: Depth of field settings that blur things in front of and behind the focus point, like a real camera lens.
CameraDOFSettings.use_dof: Turns on depth of field so only things at the focus distance are sharp and the rest is blurred.
CameraDOFSettings.focus_subtarget: The name of a bone to focus on. The camera keeps that bone sharp.
CameraDOFSettings.focus_distance: How far from the camera things are perfectly sharp. Things nearer or farther get blurrier.
CameraDOFSettings.aperture_fstop: Lens opening size. Low numbers (1.4) give strong blur, high numbers (16) keep everything sharp.
CameraDOFSettings.aperture_blades: Number of blades in the lens opening. It sets the polygon shape of blurry highlights. Minimum 3.
CameraDOFSettings.aperture_rotation: Turns the polygon shape of the blurry highlights (bokeh) around.
CameraDOFSettings.aperture_ratio: Stretches the bokeh shape. Above 1 gives tall ovals like anamorphic movie lenses, below 1 wide ones.

PointLight._: A point light, a glowing spot that shines in every direction, with its color, brightness and shadow settings.
PointLight.use_fake_user: Keeps this item saved in the file even if nothing uses it. Without it, unused items are deleted when you save and reopen.
PointLight.use_extra_user: An internal flag that marks the item as having one more user. Normally you never need to touch it.
PointLight.is_runtime_data: Marks data that Blender builds while running and does not save in the .blend file. Mostly for add-on developers.
PointLight.tag: A scratch flag that tools use to mark data for their own work. Its starting value is not reliable, so ignore it.
PointLight.type: Chooses the kind of light: where it comes from and how it spreads.
PointLight.type.POINT: Light shining in all directions from one spot, like a bare bulb.
PointLight.type.SUN: Parallel rays from very far away, like the sun. Position does not matter, only direction.
PointLight.type.SPOT: A cone of light, like a flashlight or stage spotlight.
PointLight.type.AREA: Light coming from a flat shape, like a window or softbox. Gives soft, natural shadows.
PointLight.use_temperature: Sets the light color from a temperature in Kelvin instead of picking a color.
PointLight.temperature: Light color in Kelvin. Low (2000) is warm orange like candles, high (10000) is cool blue.
PointLight.specular_factor: Strength of this light's shiny reflections. 0 removes highlights, higher makes them brighter.
PointLight.diffuse_factor: Strength of this light's normal surface lighting. 0 means it adds no regular light.
PointLight.transmission_factor: How much this light shines through see-through materials like glass.
PointLight.volume_factor: How much this light lights up fog and smoke. 0 hides it in volumes, higher makes beams brighter.
PointLight.use_custom_distance: Lets you set your own distance where light stops, instead of using the automatic cutoff.
PointLight.cutoff_distance: Distance at which the light fades to nothing. Lower saves render time but may look cut off.
PointLight.use_shadow: Lets this light cast shadows. Off makes everything it hits fully lit.
PointLight.exposure: Brightens or darkens the light in steps. Each +1 doubles the brightness, each -1 halves it.
PointLight.normalize: Keeps total brightness the same when you change the light's size, so bigger lights just get softer.
PointLight.use_nodes: Controls the light with shader nodes, for patterns or colors that change.
PointLight.use_soft_falloff: Fades the light near the surface of its shape so there are no hard edges where it touches objects.
PointLight.energy: How bright the light is. Low is dim, high is strong. Measured in watts.
PointLight.shadow_buffer_clip_start: Closest distance at which objects cast shadows from this light. Raise to fix shadow glitches near the light.
PointLight.shadow_soft_size: Size of the light for shadow blur. Bigger lights give soft blurry shadow edges, small ones sharp.
PointLight.shadow_filter_radius: Blurs the shadow edge to smooth jagged steps. Higher is softer but may blur details.

Material._: The look of a surface: its color, shininess, transparency and how EEVEE and the viewport treat it.

Material.use_extra_user: An internal flag that marks the item as having one more user. Normally you never need to touch it.
Material.is_runtime_data: Marks data that Blender builds while running and does not save in the .blend file. Mostly for add-on developers.
Material.tag: A scratch flag that tools use to mark data for their own work. Its starting value is not reliable, so ignore it.
Material.surface_render_method: Chooses how EEVEE handles see-through surfaces. A tradeoff between quality and features.
Material.surface_render_method.DITHERED: Transparency from noisy dots. Works with all effects, but only gray transparency.
Material.surface_render_method.BLENDED: Smooth colored transparency, but it can sort wrongly and does not work with all effects.
Material.displacement_method: Chooses how a material's height map changes the surface.
Material.displacement_method.BUMP: Fakes bumps with shading only. Fast, but the outline of the object stays flat.
Material.displacement_method.DISPLACEMENT: Really moves the surface points. Needs a mesh with enough faces (or subdivision).
Material.displacement_method.BOTH: Moves the surface and also adds finer fake bumps for small detail.
Material.blend_method: Old setting for how transparency is drawn. Use Surface Render Method instead.
Material.blend_method.OPAQUE: No transparency. The surface is solid.
Material.blend_method.CLIP: A pixel is either fully visible or fully hidden depending on a threshold. Hard edges.
Material.blend_method.HASHED: Uses noise dots to fake transparency. Works with most effects, looks grainy at low samples.
Material.blend_method.BLEND: Smooth see-through blending. Can sort incorrectly when many layers overlap.
Material.alpha_threshold: With Clip mode, parts below this opacity vanish. Low keeps more of the surface, high hides more.
Material.use_transparency_overlap: Draws several see-through layers one behind another. Can cause wrong sorting glitches.
Material.show_transparent_back: Old option to draw back faces of see-through objects. Can cause sorting glitches.
Material.use_backface_culling: Hides the back side of faces. Useful for open shapes where the inside should not show.
Material.use_backface_culling_shadow: Back sides of faces do not cast shadows. Helps with shadow glitches on thin objects.
Material.use_backface_culling_lightprobe_volume: Treats the material as one-sided when light probes capture lighting. Helps stop light leaking through walls.
Material.use_transparent_shadow: Lets a see-through material cast see-through shadows. Turn off for a faster, fully dark shadow.
Material.use_raytrace_refraction: Uses ray tracing to figure out what you see through glass, instead of only light probes. Better but slower.
Material.use_screen_refraction: Uses ray tracing to figure out what you see through glass, instead of only light probes. Better but slower.
Material.use_sss_translucency: Old option that lets light glow through skin-like materials. Now replaced by newer subsurface options.
Material.refraction_depth: How thick the object is for glass refraction. 0 turns the feature off; higher bends light as if through thicker glass.
Material.thickness_mode: Chooses the shortcut used to guess how light travels through a see-through object.
Material.thickness_mode.SPHERE: Guesses the object as a ball. Good for round things like marbles.
Material.thickness_mode.SLAB: Guesses the object as a flat slab of glass. Good for panes and bottles.
Material.use_thickness_from_shadow: Uses shadow maps to guess object thickness more accurately. Better results for subsurface and glass.
Material.volume_intersection_method: Chooses how overlapping volume shapes are handled.
Material.volume_intersection_method.FAST: Treats every face as a boundary. Quick, but overlapping volumes can look wrong.
Material.volume_intersection_method.ACCURATE: Only counts faces that really separate inside from outside. Slower but correct for overlaps.
Material.max_vertex_displacement: The biggest distance a vertex can be pushed by displacement. Too low cuts off the effect, too high wastes speed.
Material.preview_render_type: Chooses the shape used in the material preview thumbnail.
Material.preview_render_type.FLAT: Preview on a flat square plane.
Material.preview_render_type.SHADERBALL: Preview on a ball with a base and background, good for most materials.
Material.preview_render_type.CLOTH: Preview on a piece of cloth.
Material.use_preview_world: Lights the preview with your scene's world instead of the default light.
Material.pass_index: A number given to this material so render passes can isolate it for compositing masks.
Material.use_nodes: Builds the material with shader nodes. This is almost always on.
Material.paint_active_slot: Which texture is currently being painted in Texture Paint mode.
Material.paint_clone_slot: Which texture the Clone brush copies from in Texture Paint mode.
Material.diffuse_color: The base color seen in the viewport (solid mode). It does not control the final render when nodes are used.
Material.specular_color: The color of the shiny highlight in the viewport. Does not affect node-based rendering.
Material.roughness: Viewport smoothness. 0 is a sharp mirror-like shine, 1 is a dull, spread-out look.
Material.specular_intensity: How bright the shiny highlight is in the viewport. 0 none, 1 strong.
Material.metallic: How metal-like the surface looks in the viewport. 0 is plastic or wood, 1 is pure metal.
Material.line_color: The color of outlines drawn by Freestyle (line art rendering) around this material.
Material.line_priority: If two materials meet, the one with the higher number decides the line color.

Curve._: A curve made of control points, which can be a path, a tube, an outline or a flat shape.
Curve.use_fake_user: Keeps this item saved in the file even if nothing uses it. Without it, unused items are deleted when you save and reopen.
Curve.use_extra_user: An internal flag that marks the item as having one more user. Normally you never need to touch it.

Curve.tag: A scratch flag that tools use to mark data for their own work. Its starting value is not reliable, so ignore it.
Curve.path_duration: How many frames an object takes to travel the whole path. More frames means slower travel.
Curve.use_path: Turns the curve into a path that objects can travel along.
Curve.use_path_follow: Objects following the path turn to face along it, like a train on a track.
Curve.use_path_clamp: Stops followers from going past the start or end of the curve.
Curve.use_stretch: With Curve Deform, stretches the deformed object so it covers the entire curve.
Curve.use_deform_bounds: With Curve Deform, uses the object's box to limit how far it bends along the curve.
Curve.use_radius: Makes objects following the curve scale with the curve's radius at each point.
Curve.bevel_mode: Chooses the cross-section shape that gives the curve thickness.
Curve.bevel_mode.ROUND: Thickness with a round tube shape.
Curve.bevel_mode.OBJECT: Uses another curve object as the cross-section shape.
Curve.bevel_mode.PROFILE: Uses a custom drawn profile for each quarter of the cross-section.
Curve.bevel_resolution: How many segments make a quarter of the bevel circle. Low is blocky, high is smooth.
Curve.offset: Moves the curve geometry sideways, parallel to its surface direction. Makes outlines wider or thinner.
Curve.extrude: Gives the curve depth by pushing it up and down. Higher makes it thicker, 0 is flat.
Curve.bevel_depth: Thickness of the tube around the curve. 0 means no tube; higher means a fatter curve.
Curve.resolution_u: Number of points computed between control points along the curve. Higher is smoother but heavier.
Curve.resolution_v: Number of points computed in the V direction of a surface. Higher is smoother but heavier.
Curve.render_resolution_u: Smoothness along the curve at render time. 0 uses the viewport value.
Curve.render_resolution_v: Smoothness across the surface at render time. 0 uses the viewport value.
Curve.eval_time: How far along the curve (0 to path duration) followers are. Animate it to move objects along the path.
Curve.dimensions: Chooses whether the curve is flat (2D) or can also go up and down (3D).
Curve.dimensions.2D: The curve is flat, with Z locked. Good for outlines and shapes.
Curve.dimensions.3D: The curve can bend in all directions, including up and down.
Curve.fill_mode: Chooses which sides of a closed 2D curve are filled with a surface.
Curve.fill_mode.FULL: Fills both the front and the back.
Curve.fill_mode.HALF: Fills only one half of the shape, split by the curve direction.
Curve.fill_solver: Picks the method used to fill closed 2D curves with triangles.
Curve.fill_solver.SWEEP_LINE: Fast, but cannot handle curves that cross themselves.
Curve.fill_solver.CDT: Slower but reliable method that handles crossing and overlapping curves.
Curve.fill_rule: Decides which overlapped areas count as inside when filling.
Curve.fill_rule.EVEN_ODD: Areas alternate between filled and empty each time curves cross, leaving holes in overlaps.
Curve.fill_rule.NONZERO: Overlapping curves going the same direction are all filled; opposite directions make holes.
Curve.twist_mode: Chooses how the 3D curve twists as it travels.
Curve.twist_mode.Z_UP: Uses the world up direction to decide the twist. Simple, but can flip on steep curves.
Curve.twist_mode.MINIMUM: Uses the smallest overall twist along the curve. Often gives the smoothest result.
Curve.twist_mode.TANGENT: Uses the direction the curve is heading to work out the twist.
Curve.taper_radius_mode: Chooses how a taper object changes the thickness at each point.
Curve.taper_radius_mode.OVERRIDE: The taper replaces the point's own radius.
Curve.taper_radius_mode.MULTIPLY: The point's radius is multiplied by the taper.
Curve.taper_radius_mode.ADD: The taper is added on top of the point's radius.
Curve.bevel_factor_mapping_start: Chooses how the start factor measures distance along the curve.
Curve.bevel_factor_mapping_start.RESOLUTION: Measured by the number of subdivisions, so each little piece counts the same.
Curve.bevel_factor_mapping_start.SEGMENTS: Measured by segments between control points, each counted by its length.
Curve.bevel_factor_mapping_start.SPLINE: Measured by the whole spline length, from 0 to 1.
Curve.bevel_factor_mapping_end: Chooses how the end factor measures distance along the curve.
Curve.bevel_factor_mapping_end.RESOLUTION: Measured by the number of subdivisions, so each little piece counts the same.
Curve.bevel_factor_mapping_end.SEGMENTS: Measured by segments between control points, each counted by its length.
Curve.bevel_factor_mapping_end.SPLINE: Measured by the whole spline length, from 0 to 1.
Curve.twist_smooth: Smooths out sudden twists in the curve. Higher is smoother but changes the shape more.
Curve.use_fill_caps: Closes the open ends of a beveled curve with flat caps.
Curve.use_map_taper: Applies the taper to the beveled tube too, so the thickness shrinks along the curve.
Curve.use_auto_texspace: Resizes the texture box automatically to fit the curve.
Curve.texspace_location: Where the texture box sits. Moves how generated textures line up on the curve.
Curve.texspace_size: How big the texture box is. Larger stretches textures, smaller repeats them.
Curve.bevel_factor_start: Where the visible curve geometry begins. 0 is the start, 1 the end. Animate to make it grow.
Curve.bevel_factor_end: Where the visible curve geometry ends. 0 is the start, 1 the end. Animate to draw it on.

TextCurve.use_fill_caps: Closes the open ends of a beveled curve with flat caps.
TextCurve.use_map_taper: Applies the taper to the beveled tube too, so the thickness shrinks along the curve.
TextCurve.use_auto_texspace: Resizes the texture box automatically to fit the curve.
TextCurve.texspace_location: Where the texture box sits. Moves how generated textures line up on the curve.
TextCurve.texspace_size: How big the texture box is. Larger stretches textures, smaller repeats them.
TextCurve.bevel_factor_start: Where the visible curve geometry begins. 0 is the start, 1 the end. Animate to make it grow.
TextCurve.bevel_factor_end: Where the visible curve geometry ends. 0 is the start, 1 the end. Animate to draw it on.
TextCurve.align_x: Where text is lined up horizontally relative to the object center or text box.
TextCurve.align_x.LEFT: Text lines start at the left edge.
TextCurve.align_x.RIGHT: Text lines end at the right edge.
TextCurve.align_x.JUSTIFY: Spaces between words are stretched so lines fill the full width.
TextCurve.align_x.FLUSH: Like Justify, but spacing between every character is stretched, even on the last line.
TextCurve.align_y: Where text is lined up vertically relative to the object center.
TextCurve.align_y.TOP: The top of the text sits at the object center.
TextCurve.align_y.TOP_BASELINE: The baseline of the first line sits at the object center.
TextCurve.align_y.CENTER: The text block is centered up and down.
TextCurve.align_y.BOTTOM_BASELINE: The baseline of the last line sits at the object center.
TextCurve.align_y.BOTTOM: The bottom of the text sits at the object center.
TextCurve.overflow: Decides what happens when text is too long for its text box.
TextCurve.overflow.NONE: The text spills outside the box.
TextCurve.overflow.SCALE: The text shrinks so it all fits in the box.
TextCurve.overflow.TRUNCATE: Text that does not fit is cut off.
TextCurve.size: How big the letters are. Higher makes bigger text.
TextCurve.small_caps_scale: Size of small capital letters compared to normal capitals. 1 is the same size, lower is smaller.
TextCurve.space_line: Gap between lines of text. Higher spreads lines apart, lower packs them tighter.
TextCurve.space_word: Gap between words. Higher spreads words apart, lower pulls them together.
TextCurve.space_character: Gap between letters. Higher spreads letters apart, lower squeezes them together.
TextCurve.shear: Slants the letters like italics. 0 is upright, higher leans more to the right.
TextCurve.offset_x: Moves the text sideways from the object origin.
TextCurve.offset_y: Moves the text up or down from the object origin.
TextCurve.underline_position: How far below the text the underline is drawn.
TextCurve.active_textbox: Which text box is selected when the text has several boxes.
TextCurve.family: Name prefix of objects used as custom letters. Each character is looked up by that name.
TextCurve.body: The actual words shown by the text object.
TextCurve.use_fast_edit: Does not fill the letters while you edit text in Edit Mode. Faster for long texts.

Image._: A picture, movie or generated image used for textures, references or render results, and how Blender loads and saves it.
Image.use_fake_user: Keeps this item saved in the file even if nothing uses it. Without it, unused items are deleted when you save and reopen.
Image.use_extra_user: An internal flag that marks the item as having one more user. Normally you never need to touch it.
Image.is_runtime_data: Marks data that Blender builds while running and does not save in the .blend file. Mostly for add-on developers.
Image.tag: A scratch flag that tools use to mark data for their own work. Its starting value is not reliable, so ignore it.
Image.filepath: Where the image file is on your computer. Changing it reloads the image.
Image.filepath_raw: The file path of the image, changed without reloading. For scripts.
Image.file_format: The file type used when saving this image.
Image.file_format.AVIF: Modern small file type, good compression with good quality.
Image.file_format.JPEG: Small lossy photo format. Smaller files but no transparency.
Image.file_format.OPEN_EXR: High-quality format that keeps extra brightness range. Great for compositing.
Image.file_format.PNG: Lossless format with transparency. A great all-round choice.
Image.file_format.WEBP: Modern web format, small files with optional transparency.
Image.file_format.BMP: Old simple uncompressed format. Big files.
Image.file_format.CINEON: Film industry format for scanned film frames.
Image.file_format.DPX: Film and video industry format with high color depth.
Image.file_format.JPEG2000: Improved JPEG that can use higher color depth and transparency.
Image.file_format.HDR: Radiance HDR file for high dynamic range environment images.
Image.file_format.TARGA: Old game-industry format with transparency, lightly compressed.
Image.file_format.TARGA_RAW: Targa without any compression. Big files but simple.
Image.file_format.TIFF: Print and photo format with high quality and optional transparency.
Image.file_format.OPEN_EXR_MULTILAYER: OpenEXR holding many render layers and passes in one file.
Image.file_format.FFMPEG: Saves as a video file using the FFmpeg encoder.
Image.source: Tells Blender where the image data comes from.
Image.source.SEQUENCE: A numbered series of image files, played like a movie.
Image.source.GENERATED: An image made by Blender itself, like a blank color or test grid.
Image.source.VIEWER: The preview from a Viewer node in the compositor.
Image.source.TILED: A set of image tiles (UDIM) used for high-detail textures over many tiles.
Image.use_view_as_render: Shows the image with the same color look used for renders, such as Filmic or AgX.
Image.use_deinterlace: Removes comb-like line artifacts from interlaced video when loading it.
Image.use_multiview: Loads multiple views for stereoscopic 3D images when they are available.
Image.generated_type: Chooses what kind of image Blender makes when the source is Generated.
Image.generated_type.UV_GRID: A colored grid used to test how a UV map is stretched.
Image.generated_type.COLOR_GRID: An improved colored grid with labels, better for testing UV maps.
Image.generated_width: Width in pixels of the generated image. Higher is sharper but uses more memory.
Image.generated_height: Height in pixels of the generated image. Higher is sharper but uses more memory.
Image.use_generated_float: Makes the generated image use decimal numbers per pixel, which allows super bright values and HDR.
Image.generated_color: The fill color of a blank generated image.
Image.display_aspect: Stretches how the image is shown on screen. It does not change rendering.
Image.resolution: How many pixels per meter the image has. Mostly used for print size.
Image.pixels: The raw pixel values of the image as decimal numbers. For scripts.
Image.alpha_mode: Tells Blender how transparency is stored in the file so it can load and save it correctly.
Image.alpha_mode.STRAIGHT: Color and transparency stored separately. The most common and exact way.
Image.alpha_mode.PREMUL: Color already multiplied by transparency. Used by some video and game formats.
Image.alpha_mode.CHANNEL_PACKED: The alpha channel carries a different image, not transparency. Used for packed textures.
Image.alpha_mode.NONE: Ignores transparency and treats the image as fully solid.
Image.use_half_precision: Uses 16-bit decimals per color channel to save memory when rendering. Slightly less accurate.
Image.seam_margin: Pixels of extra paint added near UV seams to hide cracks. Higher hides more but can bleed.
Image.views_format: Chooses how views of a stereo 3D image are stored when loading it.
Image.views_format.INDIVIDUAL: Each eye view is its own file, named with a prefix or suffix.
Image.views_format.STEREO_3D: Both eye views are packed into a single file.

ParticleSettings._: The recipe for a particle system: how many particles, where they come from, how they move, look and make children or hair.
ParticleSettings.use_fake_user: Keeps this item saved in the file even if nothing uses it. Without it, unused items are deleted when you save and reopen.
ParticleSettings.use_extra_user: An internal flag that marks the item as having one more user. Normally you never need to touch it.
ParticleSettings.is_runtime_data: Marks data that Blender builds while running and does not save in the .blend file. Mostly for add-on developers.
ParticleSettings.tag: A scratch flag that tools use to mark data for their own work. Its starting value is not reliable, so ignore it.
ParticleSettings.active_texture_index: Which texture slot is currently selected in the particle texture list.
ParticleSettings.use_react_start_end: Lets particles that never reacted still be born at the end, so none are lost.
ParticleSettings.use_react_multiple: Lets a particle react to the event more than once.
ParticleSettings.use_regrow_hair: Regrows the hair again on every frame, so hair stays correct while the emitter moves.
ParticleSettings.show_unborn: Shows particles in the viewport before they are emitted.
ParticleSettings.use_dead: Keeps showing particles after they have died.
ParticleSettings.use_emit_random: Emits particles in random order instead of going through the faces one after another.
ParticleSettings.use_even_distribution: Spreads particles evenly using face area, so big faces get more than small ones.
ParticleSettings.use_die_on_collision: Particles disappear when they hit a collision object.
ParticleSettings.use_size_deflect: Uses the particle's size when it bounces, so big particles collide earlier.
ParticleSettings.use_rotations: Calculates how each particle turns, so instances can spin.
ParticleSettings.use_dynamic_rotation: Lets collisions and forces change how particles spin, not only the start rotation.
ParticleSettings.use_multiply_size_mass: Makes bigger particles heavier by multiplying mass by size.
ParticleSettings.use_advanced_hair: Uses full physics for hair as it grows, enabling gravity and collisions on the hair.
ParticleSettings.lock_boids_to_surface: Keeps boids (flocking creatures) walking on the surface, in 2D, instead of flying.
ParticleSettings.use_hair_bspline: Smooths hair with B-splines, so hair looks curvier with fewer segments.
ParticleSettings.invert_grid: Flips what counts as inside the object for grid particles.
ParticleSettings.hexagonal_grid: Places grid particles in a honeycomb pattern instead of squares.
ParticleSettings.apply_effector_to_children: Forces like wind also push the child particles, not only the parents.
ParticleSettings.create_long_hair_children: Makes children that behave better for long hair, such as keeping a good parting.
ParticleSettings.apply_guide_to_children: Hair guide curves also steer the children, not only the parents.
ParticleSettings.use_self_effect: Particles with force fields push other particles in the same system.
ParticleSettings.type: Chooses whether the system sends out moving particles or grows hair strands.
ParticleSettings.type.EMITTER: Particles are shot out over time and live for a while, like sparks or smoke.
ParticleSettings.type.HAIR: Particles are fixed strands that grow from the surface, like fur or grass.
ParticleSettings.emit_from: Chooses which part of the mesh particles start from.
ParticleSettings.emit_from.VERT: Particles appear on the mesh's vertices (corner points).
ParticleSettings.emit_from.FACE: Particles appear on the mesh's faces (surfaces).
ParticleSettings.emit_from.VOLUME: Particles appear anywhere inside the volume of the mesh.
ParticleSettings.distribution: Chooses how particles are spread over each face.
ParticleSettings.distribution.JIT: Particles are spaced evenly with a small random shake.
ParticleSettings.distribution.RAND: Particles are placed completely at random on the face.
ParticleSettings.distribution.GRID: Particles are placed in a regular grid pattern.
ParticleSettings.physics_type: Chooses what rules move the particles.
ParticleSettings.physics_type.NO: Particles do not move after being born. Used for static hair or scatter.
ParticleSettings.physics_type.NEWTON: Real-world physics: gravity, forces and collisions move the particles.
ParticleSettings.physics_type.KEYED: Particles travel through a list of target systems, like following keyframes.
ParticleSettings.physics_type.BOIDS: Particles act like a flock of birds, fish or other creatures that follow rules.
ParticleSettings.physics_type.FLUID: Particles act as liquid blobs, pushing and pulling each other (SPH fluid).
ParticleSettings.rotation_mode: Chooses which direction a particle's axis points as it moves.
ParticleSettings.rotation_mode.NONE: No special orientation. Particles keep their default direction.
ParticleSettings.rotation_mode.NOR: Points along the surface normal at the spot where the particle was born.
ParticleSettings.rotation_mode.NOR_TAN: Uses the surface normal and the surface tangent for a full orientation.
ParticleSettings.rotation_mode.VEL: Points in the direction the particle is moving.
ParticleSettings.rotation_mode.GLOB_X: Points along the world X axis.
ParticleSettings.rotation_mode.GLOB_Y: Points along the world Y axis.
ParticleSettings.rotation_mode.GLOB_Z: Points along the world Z axis.
ParticleSettings.rotation_mode.OB_X: Points along the emitter object's own X axis.
ParticleSettings.rotation_mode.OB_Y: Points along the emitter object's own Y axis.
ParticleSettings.rotation_mode.OB_Z: Points along the emitter object's own Z axis.
ParticleSettings.angular_velocity_mode: Chooses the axis particles spin around over time.
ParticleSettings.angular_velocity_mode.VELOCITY: Spins around the particle's direction of travel.
ParticleSettings.angular_velocity_mode.HORIZONTAL: Spins around a horizontal axis relative to its movement.
ParticleSettings.angular_velocity_mode.VERTICAL: Spins around a vertical axis relative to its movement.
ParticleSettings.angular_velocity_mode.GLOBAL_X: Spins around the world X axis.
ParticleSettings.angular_velocity_mode.GLOBAL_Y: Spins around the world Y axis.
ParticleSettings.angular_velocity_mode.GLOBAL_Z: Spins around the world Z axis.
ParticleSettings.angular_velocity_mode.RAND: Spins around a random axis for each particle.
ParticleSettings.react_event: Chooses what event of the target particles makes these particles react (get born).
ParticleSettings.react_event.DEATH: New particles appear when a target particle dies.
ParticleSettings.react_event.COLLIDE: New particles appear when a target particle hits something.
ParticleSettings.react_event.NEAR: New particles appear when a target particle gets close.
ParticleSettings.show_guide_hairs: Shows the main guide hairs that control the shape of the others.
ParticleSettings.show_hair_grid: Shows the grid used for hair simulation.
ParticleSettings.show_velocity: Draws a line for each particle showing its speed and direction.
ParticleSettings.show_size: Draws a circle around each particle showing its size.
ParticleSettings.show_health: Shows the health value of boids in the viewport.
ParticleSettings.use_absolute_path_time: Path start and end are counted in real frames instead of a 0 to 1 range.
ParticleSettings.use_parent_particles: Also renders the parent particles, not only their children.
ParticleSettings.show_number: Shows each particle's number next to it.
ParticleSettings.use_collection_pick_random: Picks objects from the collection at random for each particle.
ParticleSettings.use_collection_count: Lets the same object appear several times, using the counts you set in the list.
ParticleSettings.use_global_instance: Copies the object using its world coordinates instead of its local ones.
ParticleSettings.use_rotation_instance: Copies keep the instance object's own rotation.
ParticleSettings.use_scale_instance: Copies keep the instance object's own scale.
ParticleSettings.use_render_adaptive: Uses fewer path segments on straight parts and more on curves when rendering.
ParticleSettings.use_velocity_length: Makes each line as long as the particle's speed.
ParticleSettings.use_whole_collection: Places every object of the collection at each particle at once.
ParticleSettings.use_strand_primitive: Renders hair as thin strands, which is faster and lighter on memory.
ParticleSettings.display_method: Chooses how particles look in the viewport.
ParticleSettings.display_method.NONE: Particles are not shown in the viewport.
ParticleSettings.display_method.RENDER: Shows particles as they will render.
ParticleSettings.display_method.AXIS: Shows particles as axis arrows, showing rotation.
ParticleSettings.render_type: Chooses what each particle turns into at render time.
ParticleSettings.render_type.NONE: Nothing is rendered for the particles.
ParticleSettings.render_type.HALO: Each particle renders as a little glowing point.
ParticleSettings.render_type.LINE: Each particle renders as a line along its movement.
ParticleSettings.render_type.PATH: Particles render as paths, used for hair and strands.
ParticleSettings.render_type.OBJECT: Each particle is replaced by a copy of an object you pick.
ParticleSettings.render_type.COLLECTION: Each particle is replaced by objects from a collection.
ParticleSettings.display_color: Colors particles in the viewport using extra data.
ParticleSettings.display_color.NONE: No extra color. Particles use the normal display color.
ParticleSettings.display_color.MATERIAL: Particles use the color of their material.
ParticleSettings.display_color.VELOCITY: Color shows how fast each particle is moving.
ParticleSettings.display_color.ACCELERATION: Color shows how fast each particle's speed is changing.
ParticleSettings.display_size: How big particles appear in the viewport. Only for display, not render.
ParticleSettings.child_type: Chooses how child particles are created from parents.
ParticleSettings.child_type.NONE: No children. Only the main particles exist.
ParticleSettings.child_type.SIMPLE: Children are copies placed around each parent. Fast and simple.
ParticleSettings.child_type.INTERPOLATED: Children are blended between nearby parents. Looks more natural for hair.
ParticleSettings.display_step: Detail of paths in the viewport, as a power of 2. Higher is smoother but slower.
ParticleSettings.render_step: Detail of paths when rendering, as a power of 2. Higher is smoother but slower.
ParticleSettings.hair_step: Number of segments in each hair strand. More gives smoother curves but heavier hair.
ParticleSettings.bending_random: Random variation in how stiff each hair is. Higher makes hairs bend more differently.
ParticleSettings.keys_step: Internal step setting for keyed path points. Rarely needs changing.
ParticleSettings.adaptive_angle: Degrees a path must bend before another render segment is added. Lower is smoother and heavier.
ParticleSettings.adaptive_pixel: Pixels a path must cover before another render segment is added. Lower is smoother and heavier.
ParticleSettings.display_percentage: Percent of particles shown in the viewport. Lower makes the viewport faster, render is unchanged.
ParticleSettings.material: Number of the material slot used on the particles when rendering.
ParticleSettings.material_slot: The material slot used to render the particles.
ParticleSettings.material_slot.DEFAULT: Uses the default first material slot.
ParticleSettings.integrator: The math method used to move particles. Faster ones are less exact; slower ones are more stable.
ParticleSettings.integrator.EULER: Simplest and fastest. Least accurate and can become unstable.
ParticleSettings.integrator.VERLET: Stable for hair and for particles under constant force.
ParticleSettings.integrator.MIDPOINT: A balanced method, more accurate than Euler.
ParticleSettings.integrator.RK4: Slowest and most accurate and stable method.
ParticleSettings.kink: Chooses a pattern that makes hair or paths curl and wave.
ParticleSettings.kink.CURL: Hair curls around itself in a spiral.
ParticleSettings.kink.RADIAL: Hair bends outward from the center like a fan.
ParticleSettings.kink.WAVE: Hair makes a wavy S shape.
ParticleSettings.kink.BRAID: Hair weaves in a braid pattern.
ParticleSettings.kink.SPIRAL: Hair spirals out like a coil that grows wider.
ParticleSettings.kink_axis: Chooses the axis around which the kink pattern happens.
ParticleSettings.kink_axis.X: The kink pattern happens around the X axis.
ParticleSettings.kink_axis.Y: The kink pattern happens around the Y axis.
ParticleSettings.kink_axis.Z: The kink pattern happens around the Z axis.
ParticleSettings.color_maximum: The value that matches the strongest color when particles are colored by velocity or acceleration.
ParticleSettings.frame_start: The animation frame when particles start being emitted.
ParticleSettings.frame_end: The animation frame when particles stop being emitted.
ParticleSettings.lifetime: How many frames each particle lives before it dies. Higher keeps particles around longer.
ParticleSettings.lifetime_random: Random variation of the lifetime. 0 gives all the same lifetime, 1 varies a lot.
ParticleSettings.time_tweak: Speeds up or slows down particle physics. 1 is normal, 2 is double speed, 0.5 is slow motion.
ParticleSettings.timestep: Seconds of simulation per frame. Lower is more accurate but slower.
ParticleSettings.use_adaptive_subframes: Automatically picks how many sub-steps per frame the simulation needs.
ParticleSettings.subframes: Extra simulation steps per frame. More steps make fast particles more stable but slow things down.
ParticleSettings.courant_target: How far a particle can move before more subframes are added. Lower is more careful and slower.
ParticleSettings.jitter_factor: How much random shake is added to particle placement. 0 is perfectly even, 1 is very uneven.
ParticleSettings.effect_hair: How stiff hair is when force fields push it. Higher resists forces more.
ParticleSettings.count: Total number of particles or hair strands. More looks fuller but is heavier.
ParticleSettings.userjit: How many particles per face when using Jittered distribution. 0 picks automatically.
ParticleSettings.grid_resolution: Number of grid points along each side for grid placement. Higher gives more particles.
ParticleSettings.grid_random: Random offset of grid points. 0 is a neat grid, higher is messier.
ParticleSettings.effector_amount: How many particles act as force effectors. 0 means all of them.
ParticleSettings.normal_factor: Speed along the surface normal at birth. Higher shoots particles outward faster.
ParticleSettings.object_factor: How much of the emitter's movement the particles inherit. Higher carries them along.
ParticleSettings.factor_random: Random variation of the start speed. 0 is the same for all, higher is more random.
ParticleSettings.particle_factor: Start speed taken from the target particle. Higher makes them follow it more.
ParticleSettings.tangent_factor: Start speed along the surface, sideways to the normal. Higher swirls particles along the surface.
ParticleSettings.tangent_phase: Turns the tangent direction around the normal, changing the sideways direction.
ParticleSettings.reactor_factor: Start speed pointing away from the target particle. Higher pushes them further away.
ParticleSettings.object_align_factor: Start speed in the emitter's direction. Higher shoots along the emitter axes.
ParticleSettings.angular_velocity_factor: How fast particles spin, in radians per second. 0 is no spin, higher is faster.
ParticleSettings.phase_factor: Starting twist around the chosen orientation axis.
ParticleSettings.rotation_factor_random: Random start orientation. 0 keeps all aligned, 1 points every particle somewhere else.
ParticleSettings.phase_factor_random: Random twist around the orientation axis. Higher gives more varied rotations.
ParticleSettings.hair_length: How long hair strands are. Higher grows longer hair.
ParticleSettings.mass: How heavy each particle is. Heavier particles resist forces more.
ParticleSettings.particle_size: How big each particle is. Higher gives bigger particles or instances.
ParticleSettings.size_random: Random variation of particle size. 0 same size, 1 big differences.
ParticleSettings.drag_factor: Air resistance slowing particles. 0 is none, higher slows them quickly.
ParticleSettings.brownian_factor: Random jitter in movement. Higher makes particles wander like dust.
ParticleSettings.damping: Slows particles by friction. 0 is none, 1 stops them quickly.
ParticleSettings.length_random: Random variation of path length. Higher makes strands different lengths.
ParticleSettings.child_percent: Number of children per parent in the viewport. More children make fuller hair, but are slower.
ParticleSettings.rendered_child_count: Number of children per parent when rendering. Usually higher than the viewport count.
ParticleSettings.virtual_parents: How many hidden extra parents are used for interpolation. Higher makes more varied children.
ParticleSettings.child_size: Size multiplier for the children. 1 same as parent, lower smaller.
ParticleSettings.child_size_random: Random variation in child size. Higher makes sizes more different.
ParticleSettings.child_radius: How far children spread out around each parent. Higher makes a wider cloud.
ParticleSettings.child_roundness: Shape of the child area. 0 is flat, 1 is round around the parent.
ParticleSettings.clump_factor: How strongly children pull toward their parent. Positive clumps tips together, negative spreads them.
ParticleSettings.clump_shape: Shapes the clumping. Below 0 clumps near the root, above 0 near the tip.
ParticleSettings.use_clump_curve: Uses a drawn curve to control how clumping changes along the hair.
ParticleSettings.use_clump_noise: Makes random clumps around the parent for a messier look.
ParticleSettings.clump_noise_size: Size of the random clumps. Smaller gives many tiny clumps, larger gives big ones.
ParticleSettings.kink_amplitude: How far the kink pattern pushes away from the straight line. Higher is a bigger curl.
ParticleSettings.kink_amplitude_clump: How much clumping reduces the kink size. Higher makes clumped hair curl less.
ParticleSettings.kink_amplitude_random: Random variation of kink size. Higher gives hairs with different sized curls.
ParticleSettings.kink_frequency: How many times the pattern repeats along the hair. Higher is tighter waves.
ParticleSettings.kink_shape: Moves the kink pattern toward the root or the tip of the hair.
ParticleSettings.kink_flat: How flat the kink is. 0 is a round spiral, 1 is flat like a zigzag.
ParticleSettings.kink_extra_steps: Extra detail points for special kink shapes like braids. Higher is smoother but heavier.
ParticleSettings.kink_axis_random: Random variation of the direction of the kink axis. Higher gives more chaos.
ParticleSettings.roughness_1: Amount of smooth, repeating roughness based on location. Higher gives more wobble.
ParticleSettings.roughness_1_size: Size of the location-based roughness. Small is fine wobble, large is gentle waves.
ParticleSettings.roughness_2: Amount of random roughness for each strand. Higher is messier.
ParticleSettings.roughness_2_size: Size of the random roughness. Small makes fine fuzz, large makes loose waves.
ParticleSettings.roughness_2_threshold: Share of strands the random roughness skips. Higher leaves more strands clean.
ParticleSettings.roughness_endpoint: Extra roughness at the tip of the strands. Higher makes frayed ends.
ParticleSettings.roughness_end_shape: Shape of the end roughness. Moves how far from the tip it begins.
ParticleSettings.use_roughness_curve: Uses a drawn curve to control roughness along the hair.
ParticleSettings.child_length: Length of the children compared to parents. 1 same length, lower shorter.
ParticleSettings.child_length_threshold: Share of children left at full length. Others get shortened.
ParticleSettings.child_parting_factor: Splits children into parted sections following the parents, like a hair parting.
ParticleSettings.child_parting_min: Smallest angle between root and tip used for parting.
ParticleSettings.child_parting_max: Largest angle between root and tip used for parting.
ParticleSettings.branch_threshold: How many children become branches. Higher branches more.
ParticleSettings.line_length_tail: Length of the tail of a line-rendered particle. Higher makes a longer trail behind.
ParticleSettings.line_length_head: Length of the head of a line-rendered particle. Higher extends the line forward.
ParticleSettings.path_start: When the path starts being drawn. 0 is the start of its life.
ParticleSettings.path_end: When the path stops being drawn. 1 is the end of its life.
ParticleSettings.trail_count: Number of copies trailing behind each particle. Higher makes a longer trail.
ParticleSettings.keyed_loops: How many times the keyed targets are repeated.
ParticleSettings.use_modifier_stack: Emits from the mesh after modifiers are applied. Use the same subdivision level in viewport and render.
ParticleSettings.active_instanceweight_index: Which object in the instance list is currently selected.
ParticleSettings.twist: How many turns hair strands twist around the parent. Higher gives a tighter twist.
ParticleSettings.use_twist_curve: Uses a drawn curve to control the twist along the strand.
ParticleSettings.use_close_tip: Makes the tip of every strand shrink to a point.
ParticleSettings.shape: Shapes how thick the strand is along its length. Below 0 is thicker at the root, above 0 at the tip.
ParticleSettings.root_radius: Thickness of a strand at the root. Higher gives thicker hair.
ParticleSettings.tip_radius: Thickness of a strand at the tip. Higher gives blunt tips, 0 a point.
ParticleSettings.radius_scale: Multiplier for all strand thickness values. Higher makes every strand thicker.

ParticleSystem._: The live particle system on an object, with its random seeds, hair dynamics and the vertex groups that paint where effects apply.
ParticleSystem.use_fake_user: Keeps this item saved in the file even if nothing uses it. Without it, unused items are deleted when you save and reopen.
ParticleSystem.use_extra_user: An internal flag that marks the item as having one more user. Normally you never need to touch it.
ParticleSystem.is_runtime_data: Marks data that Blender builds while running and does not save in the .blend file. Mostly for add-on developers.
ParticleSystem.tag: A scratch flag that tools use to mark data for their own work. Its starting value is not reliable, so ignore it.
ParticleSystem.seed: Changes the random pattern. Try another number to get a different random result with the same settings.
ParticleSystem.child_seed: Changes the random pattern of the child particles only. Try another number for a different look.
ParticleSystem.use_hair_dynamics: Lets the hair swing and flop using the cloth simulation, instead of staying stiff.
ParticleSystem.reactor_target_particle_system: For reactor systems, the number of the particle system on the target object to react to.
ParticleSystem.use_keyed_timing: Uses the times you set on each key target instead of splitting the time evenly.
ParticleSystem.active_particle_target_index: Which target is currently selected in the target list.
ParticleSystem.vertex_group_density: Name of a vertex group that paints how many particles appear. Heavier paint means a stronger effect, none means zero.
ParticleSystem.invert_vertex_group_density: Flips the group, so unpainted areas get the effect on how many particles appear and painted areas get none.
ParticleSystem.vertex_group_velocity: Name of a vertex group that paints how fast they start. Heavier paint means a stronger effect, none means zero.
ParticleSystem.invert_vertex_group_velocity: Flips the group, so unpainted areas get the effect on how fast they start and painted areas get none.
ParticleSystem.vertex_group_length: Name of a vertex group that paints how long hair is. Heavier paint means a stronger effect, none means zero.
ParticleSystem.invert_vertex_group_length: Flips the group, so unpainted areas get the effect on how long hair is and painted areas get none.
ParticleSystem.vertex_group_clump: Name of a vertex group that paints how much hair clumps. Heavier paint means a stronger effect, none means zero.
ParticleSystem.invert_vertex_group_clump: Flips the group, so unpainted areas get the effect on how much hair clumps and painted areas get none.
ParticleSystem.vertex_group_kink: Name of a vertex group that paints how much hair curls. Heavier paint means a stronger effect, none means zero.
ParticleSystem.invert_vertex_group_kink: Flips the group, so unpainted areas get the effect on how much hair curls and painted areas get none.
ParticleSystem.vertex_group_roughness_1: Name of a vertex group that paints the first roughness. Heavier paint means a stronger effect, none means zero.
ParticleSystem.invert_vertex_group_roughness_1: Flips the group, so unpainted areas get the effect on the first roughness and painted areas get none.
ParticleSystem.vertex_group_roughness_2: Name of a vertex group that paints the second roughness. Heavier paint means a stronger effect, none means zero.
ParticleSystem.invert_vertex_group_roughness_2: Flips the group, so unpainted areas get the effect on the second roughness and painted areas get none.
ParticleSystem.vertex_group_roughness_end: Name of a vertex group that paints the roughness at the tips. Heavier paint means a stronger effect, none means zero.
ParticleSystem.invert_vertex_group_roughness_end: Flips the group, so unpainted areas get the effect on the roughness at the tips and painted areas get none.
ParticleSystem.vertex_group_size: Name of a vertex group that paints how big particles are. Heavier paint means a stronger effect, none means zero.
ParticleSystem.invert_vertex_group_size: Flips the group, so unpainted areas get the effect on how big particles are and painted areas get none.
ParticleSystem.vertex_group_tangent: Name of a vertex group that paints the sideways start speed. Heavier paint means a stronger effect, none means zero.
ParticleSystem.invert_vertex_group_tangent: Flips the group, so unpainted areas get the effect on the sideways start speed and painted areas get none.
ParticleSystem.vertex_group_rotation: Name of a vertex group that paints how they are rotated. Heavier paint means a stronger effect, none means zero.
ParticleSystem.invert_vertex_group_rotation: Flips the group, so unpainted areas get the effect on how they are rotated and painted areas get none.
ParticleSystem.vertex_group_field: Name of a vertex group that paints how strong force fields act. Heavier paint means a stronger effect, none means zero.
ParticleSystem.invert_vertex_group_field: Flips the group, so unpainted areas get the effect on how strong force fields act and painted areas get none.
ParticleSystem.vertex_group_twist: Name of a vertex group that paints how much hair twists. Heavier paint means a stronger effect, none means zero.
ParticleSystem.invert_vertex_group_twist: Flips the group, so unpainted areas get the effect on how much hair twists and painted areas get none.

RigidBodyObject._: How one object behaves in the rigid body physics simulation: whether it falls, how heavy, bouncy and slippery it is.
RigidBodyObject.type: Chooses whether physics moves the object or you do.
RigidBodyObject.type.ACTIVE: The simulation moves the object. It falls, bounces and gets pushed around.
RigidBodyObject.type.PASSIVE: The object stays where you animate it. It acts as a fixed floor or wall that active objects hit.
RigidBodyObject.mesh_source: Chooses which version of the mesh is used to build the collision shape.
RigidBodyObject.mesh_source.BASE: Uses the original mesh with no changes.
RigidBodyObject.mesh_source.DEFORM: Uses the mesh after shape keys and deforming modifiers.
RigidBodyObject.mesh_source.FINAL: Uses the mesh after all modifiers are applied.
RigidBodyObject.enabled: Lets the object take part in the simulation. Off makes it ignored by physics.
RigidBodyObject.collision_shape: The simple shape used for collisions. Simpler shapes simulate faster.
RigidBodyObject.collision_shape.BOX: A box. Fast and fine for cubes and flat floors.
RigidBodyObject.collision_shape.SPHERE: A ball. Very fast and good for round objects.
RigidBodyObject.collision_shape.CAPSULE: A pill shape, like a cylinder with round ends. Good for characters.
RigidBodyObject.collision_shape.CYLINDER: A can shape. Good for poles and barrels.
RigidBodyObject.collision_shape.CONVEX_HULL: A shrink-wrapped outline around the mesh with no dents. Good balance of speed and accuracy.
RigidBodyObject.collision_shape.MESH: Uses the real triangle mesh, so dents and holes count. Most exact but slow, and best for passive objects.
RigidBodyObject.collision_shape.COMPOUND: Joins all its rigid body children into one shape, so the group moves as one.
RigidBodyObject.kinematic: Lets animation move an active object. Physics still reacts to it but cannot move it.
RigidBodyObject.use_deform: Allows the object to bend and deform during the simulation.
RigidBodyObject.mass: How heavy the object is. Heavy objects are harder to push, light ones fly easily.
RigidBodyObject.use_deactivation: Lets objects at rest go to sleep to save time. Faster, but sleeping objects may not wake on small touches.
RigidBodyObject.use_start_deactivated: The object begins asleep and wakes up when something hits it.
RigidBodyObject.deactivate_linear_velocity: Speed below which the object can go to sleep. Higher puts it to sleep sooner.
RigidBodyObject.deactivate_angular_velocity: Spin speed below which the object can go to sleep. Higher puts it to sleep sooner.
RigidBodyObject.linear_damping: How quickly the object loses movement speed, like air drag. 0 keeps moving, 1 stops fast.
RigidBodyObject.angular_damping: How quickly the object loses spin. 0 keeps spinning, 1 stops fast.
RigidBodyObject.friction: How much the surface grips. 0 is like ice, 1 or more is like rubber.
